items.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 22 at 6:46PM PST until November 25 at 3:00AM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
items.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor to moderate
coastal flooding is expected. For the Coastal Flood Watch,
significant coastal flooding is possible. Most susceptible
time of flooding will be around the time of the morning high
tides between about 730 AM and 930 AM, especially Wednesday
and Thursday.

* WHERE...Ventura County Beaches.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 AM Monday to 3
AM PST Wednesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from late
Tuesday night through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...There is the potential for damaging flooding of sea
water over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially
around the time of high tide, including over beaches, roads,
and structures including piers. Significant beach erosion is
possible. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large
breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and
rocks, and capsize small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Highest risk likely Wednesday and
Thursday with potential for significant impacts. Elevated to
high surf is expected much of the week, with even the
possibility of warning- level surf at times from Wednesday
afternoon into Thursday. Additional products will likely be
needed into Friday.
items.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Plan
for extra travel time as some roads may be closed.

items.headline: Marine Weather Statement issued November 23 at 3:27AM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
items.description:
RISK OF BREAKING WAVES IN THE MORRO BAY AND VENTURA HARBOR
ENTRRANCES EARLY WEDNESDAY MORNING THROUGH THURSDAY AFTERNOON

A large and long period westerly swell will produce a risk of
breaking waves in the Morro Bay and Ventura Harbor entrances
early Wednesday morning through Thursday afternoon. These
conditions have a history of capsizing vessels of various sizes
resulting in serious injury or death, even to the most experienced
mariners.

Mariners are urged to stay clear of these harbor entrances during
the time mentioned. For more information, contact the local
harbor patrol or coast guard station and continue to monitor NOAA
Weather Radio for the latest weather information.
